SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::svd_u¶

Back to SeriesLinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::svd_u(bool full_matrices = true) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::svd_u(bool full_matrices = true) const

What It Does¶

svd_u() returns the left singular vectors: orthonormal output-space directions in A = U diag(S) Vh. Column i is the direction produced when the matching right singular direction is transformed and scaled by S_i.

Use svd_u() when downstream work needs only an orthonormal basis for the matrix’s output or column space. Typical uses include projecting output-space observations, comparing learned subspaces, or retaining leading output directions. Use svd() when U must be paired with singular values or right singular vectors.

Calling Styles And Which One To Use¶

auto direct = matrix.linearalg.svd_u(false);    // SeriesLinearAlgAccessor
auto proxied = matrix.linearalg().svd_u(false); // SeriesLinearAlgProxy

Both calls decompose matrix. The proxy is merely a lightweight unary wrapper bound to the accessor’s owner; it does not represent a different U or a different algorithm. Prefer the direct accessor spelling. Peer binding through linearalg(other) is for binary operations and is unnecessary here.

Directions In The Output Space¶

Reduced U describes only directions reached by the represented map. Full U extends those columns to a complete orthonormal basis, including output-space directions that do not participate in reconstructing a tall matrix.

Parameter And Shape¶

For [...,m,n] and k=min(m,n), full_matrices=true returns [...,m,m]; false returns [...,m,k].

Returns¶

Series The left singular-vector matrix. Columns are ordered to match descending singular values. The method returns the component directly, unlike svd(), where the same value is available as .u.

Gradient¶

Use full_matrices=false for reverse mode. Gradients through singular vectors are unstable at repeated or nearly repeated singular values because no unique basis exists within the tied subspace.

Examples¶

Example 1. Reduced and full mode answer different basis questions for a tall matrix.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 0.0}, {0.0, 2.0}, {0.0, 0.0}});
std::cout << "reduced=" << a.linearalg.svd_u(false) << "\n";
std::cout << "full=" << a.linearalg.svd_u() << "\n";

Output¶

reduced=pluss::Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0],
  [0, 1],
  [0, 0]]
full=pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 0],
  [0, 1, 0],
  [0, 0, 1]]

Reduced U spans the represented two-dimensional column space. Full U adds the third orthogonal direction needed to span the complete output space.

Example 2. Validate U through orthonormality, not exact signs.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {1.0, 3.0}});
auto u = matrix.linearalg.svd_u(false);
std::cout << u.transpose(0, 1).linearalg.mm(u) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 1.9967346e-16],
  [1.9967346e-16, 1]]

Example 3. Reverse mode can differentiate a reduced singular-vector objective.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {0.0, 2.0}});
matrix.tracks_slope_(true);
matrix.linearalg.svd_u(false).sum().reverse();
std::cout << matrix.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.13374653, -0.089164353],
  [-0.2006198, -0.15603762]]

This example uses distinct singular values. At a tie, the individual columns can rotate inside their shared subspace, so this derivative is not unique.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • A column and its matching row in Vh may both change sign without changing A.

  • Full mode adds basis vectors that are not needed for reconstruction.

  • Do not compare singular vectors element by element when validating a decomposition.

  • svd_u() returns a Series; svd() returns the same coordinated component in its .u field.

Summary¶

Use svd_u(false) for the compact orthonormal basis of the output/column space. Request full mode only when a complete output-space basis is required, and use joint svd() when directions must remain paired with strengths.

See Also¶

  • svd: obtain coordinated factors.

  • svd_vh: input-space singular directions.
